title: US midterms 2026: from election night to a new Congress
dek: The results so far, the races still being counted, and what changes when the new Congress meets in January.
bigLabel: Democratic House seats won in AP's count as of 13 Nov, 1:16 pm IST, against 169 for Republicans. Counts may change.

glance.what: Americans voted on 3 November for all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats. As of 13 November, AP's count shows Democrats with 255 House seats won and Republicans with 169, and 55 Senate seats for Democrats (including 2 who caucus with them) against 44 for Republicans.
glance.why: Congress writes US spending and trade laws and confirms judges and officials, so the result shapes the last two years of President Trump's term, including tariff fights that matter to Indian exporters.
glance.next: All Senate races have now been called by AP. AP called Tennessee's 4th House district on 24 November; Roll Call says three House races remain, two Louisiana runoffs in December and a recount in Minnesota's 1st district. States are certifying results. The new Congress is due to meet in early January 2027.

forYou: For India, the result matters most through trade: tariffs, the unsigned India–US deal and sanctions on Russian oil all pass through Washington. Commerce ministry sources say the result will not affect the interim trade deal.

events.title: Election day, record midterm turnout
events.summary: Voters choose all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats, plus governors. More than 124 million ballots are cast, above the previous midterm record of nearly 119 million in 2018, according to the University of Florida Election Lab.

events.title: Seven Senate seats flip, including Texas
events.summary: Senate seats in North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Kansas, Iowa and Maine flip from Republican to Democratic, NPR reports. Races in Mississippi and Alaska are too close to call on 4 November. The campaign was dominated by the cost of living.
events.status: Reported · NPR, based on AP race calls

events.title: Trump: 'I have total veto power'
events.summary: President Trump tells The New York Times that he has veto power over legislation and is open to good ideas. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer calls the results a 'generational remake' of the Senate map.

events.title: Where the count stands
events.summary: As of 1:16 pm IST on 13 November, AP's count shows Democrats with 255 House seats won and Republicans with 169; 11 House seats are not yet counted as won for either party. In the Senate, Democrats have 55 seats including 2 who caucus with them, and Republicans 44; 1 seat is not yet counted for either. These numbers may change.

events.title: AP calls Alaska's Senate race for Peltola, the last Senate race to be decided
events.summary: The Associated Press called Alaska's US Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola over Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan on the evening of 17 November, Alaska time. In the latest count Peltola had 144,302 votes (50.12%) to Sullivan's 131,844, Alaska's News Source reports. Because she passed 50%, Alaska's ranked-choice second round was not needed. AP says it was the last Senate race of the midterms to be decided. Sullivan's campaign said it would not comment until all ballots were counted. The result has not yet been certified.

events.title: Van Hollen claims growing support in his challenge to Schumer; Trump weighs in
events.summary: Senator Chris Van Hollen, who launched a challenge to Chuck Schumer for leader of the Senate Democrats on 12 November, told NBC's Meet the Press that more than 15 senators back him, per Newsweek and HNGN. Newsweek's count of public statements has at least 16 senators backing Schumer and 6 backing Van Hollen. The vote is a secret ballot on 1 December; 28 of 55 eligible senators-elect are needed to win. On Truth Social, President Trump wrote: "It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority Leader."
events.differs: HNGN gives two different public counts, 15 to 5 and 16 to 6, for Schumer and Van Hollen.

events.title: AP calls North Carolina's 5th district for Democrat Chuck Hubbard after a recount
events.summary: AP called North Carolina's 5th House district for Democrat Chuck Hubbard after a recount, per ABC News. The seat had been held by Republican Virginia Foxx since 2005. Foxx conceded on Sunday, writing that voters "made their voices heard", per WRAL. Before the recount Hubbard led by 331 votes out of more than 286,000, in the unofficial state count. Some other House races are still being counted.

events.title: AP calls Tennessee's 4th district for Democrat Victoria Broderick
events.summary: The Associated Press called Tennessee's 4th House district for Democrat Victoria Broderick over Republican Rep. Scott DesJarlais at 11:12 am Central time on 24 November, per NewsChannel 9. She led by 361 votes when the race was called, Roll Call reports, three weeks after election day. DesJarlais had already said his campaign finished "just a few hundred votes short". Roll Call says three House races are still not called, including two Louisiana seats going to December runoffs and Minnesota's 1st district, which is heading for a hand recount.
